description.narrative:
Ambassaden har fått en förfrågan av ECOWAS att finansiera projektet "Transitional Support to the ECOWAS Regional Radio" med 11,2 miljoner kronor under perioden juli 2018 till september 2019.
Huvudsyftet med stödet är att tillhandahålla övergångsstöd till ECOWAS Radio som syftar till att bidra till främjandet av lokala fredsbyggande initiativ i Liberia, samtidigt som radions kapacitet stärks för att garantera en smidig expansion till samtliga 15 medlemsländerna i ECOWAS.
Stödet förväntas bidra till att: - ECOWAS förstärker sin operativa kapacitet att arbeta med radiosändning samtidigt som organisationen utvecklar sin kapacitet att expandera sina radiofaciliteter till alla 15 medlemsstater i Västafrika. -ECOWAS använder radio för att skapa strategiska partnerskap med civilsamhällesorganisationer, media och allmänheten för att skapa en plattform för främjande av fred och utveckling i Liberia.
Insatsen förlängdes 2022-2024, i syfte att 1) erbjuda neutral nyhetssrapportering under valåret 2023, 2) implementera specifika insatser för att säkra fortsatt nyhetsrapportering efter att de migrerat till en regional station, i form av kunskapsöverföring till och solarisering av sk. Community Radio Stations

ECOWAS has applied to The Embassy of Sweden for funding of 11,2 million SEK to carry out the “Transitional Support to the ECOWAS Regional Radio” during July 2018 to September 2019.
The main objective of the intervention is to provide transitional support to the ECOWAS radio that will contribute to the promotion of local peacebuilding initiatives in Liberia, while building the capacity of the radio to guarantee a smooth expansion to cover the 15 countries in the West African sub-region.
Two main outcomes are expected to be achieved by the intervention: - ECOWAS solidifies its operational capability to maintain broadcast of its radio station while developing its capacity to expand its radio facilities to all 15 countries in West Africa; and -ECOWAS Utilizes radio programming to establish strategic partnerships with civil society organizations, other media/communication institutions, and the public so as to create a reliable platform for the promotion of peace and development in Liberia.
The contribution was extended 2022-2024 in order to 1) ensure unbiased and non-partisan news reporting during the election year 2023, and 2) implement a proper exit-strategy including transfer of knowledge to and solarising of Community Radio Stations

The main objective of the intervention is to provide transitional support to ECOWAS Radio. By providing an independant radio station with national coverage, ECOWAS contributes to the promotion of local peacebuilding initiatives in Liberia, while building the capacity of the Radio to guarantee a smooth expansion to cover the 15 countries in the West African sub-region.
Two main outcomes are expected to be achieved by this intervention:
ECOWAS solidifies its operational capability to maintain broadcast of its Radio station while developing its capacity to expand its radio facilities to all 15 countries in West Africa;
ECOWAS utilizes Radio programming to establish strategic partnerships with civil society organizations, other media/communication institutions, and the public so as to create a reliable platform for the promotion of peace and development in Liberia
ECOWAS have decided on a final exit strategy for 2022-2024 during which they plan to transfer their skills and knowledge to the Association of Liberian Community Radio Stations (ALICOR), while ensuring that unbiased radio broadcasting is available nation-wide during elections.

description.narrative:
The initiative significantly expanded access to reliable, nonpartisan information across Liberia, providing nationwide news and programming that proved especially valuable during the 2023 elections through neutral and credible reporting. Daily broadcasts promoted peace, sustainable development, and fact-based public information.
Support to community radio stations strengthened media capacity nationwide. Around 30 stations improved their production skills, and financial assistance increased access to information in rural areas. Training on conflict sensitive reporting reached stations in 15 counties, while peace focused listening circles in conflict prone and hard-to-reach areas encouraged community led conflict prevention and resolution. The installation of solar power in 14 stations improved broadcasting reliability, enabling some such as VRM community radio to operate nearly 24 hours.
Targeted support to ALICOR included an internship programme for 20 producers and solar power installation, further strengthening the associations operational capacity.
During the COVID19 pandemic, ECOWAS Radio played a key role in public awareness efforts through radio programming, theatre, and street performances.
